$comment: KNOWN-RED LEDGER (B266080). The e2e cases that are failing today and are NOT being fixed
in the run that recorded them. scripts/e2e-drift-gate.mjs compares each run against this
list and fails on EITHER side: a failure that is not listed is a NEW regression, and a
listed case that PASSES means the ledger is stale and must shrink.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The E2E workflow was red on 17 consecutive scheduled runs (every
weekday from 2026-07-22; last green 2026-07-21) and filed correctly every time — as 12
comments on one idempotently-reused issue (#762) that nobody answered for 17 days. The
alarm was not noisy, it was MUTE, and while every run was red a brand-new regression
would have changed nothing about the signal anyone saw. A list in the repo is reviewable;
a comment on a muted thread is not.
TWO LANES, because the two configurations do not see the same thing:
ci    — the scheduled workflow: SIGNED IN, against production planyr.io.
local — `npm run e2e` with no BASE_URL: LOGGED OUT, against a local build of the tree.
Measured head-to-head 2026-08-08 (ci run #41: 30 red · a full local sweep: 33 red):
25 red in BOTH  ·  5 red only in ci  ·  8 red only in local.
The 25 matter because they say these failures are NOT production or auth noise — they
reproduce on a plain local build with no account, so they are real and anyone can fix them.
The 13 that differ matter because neither lane substitutes for the other, so a case red in
one lane is no evidence at all about the other and the gate never lets one lane's entry
silence the other's failure. That gap is exactly how B1179's click-behavior and
inspector-close cases ended up with no watcher anywhere.
THE COUNT IS THE DEBT. It may fall freely; it grows only with --allow-grow --item B###.
The ci lane was seeded from run #41 (2026-08-07, 30 failed / 312 passed / 1 flaky).
module-keepalive's 'hidden headers ignore f' case was on this list at seeding and has been
REMOVED because it was fixed in the same change (B1179): the step that pressed Escape to
leave REAL browser fullscreen was written for the old chrome-hide `f` and headless Chromium
has no browser chrome to answer it. A fixed case never keeps its amnesty — that is the half
of the gate that stops this file becoming a permanent one.
THE LOCAL LANE was seeded from a full sweep run in the development sandbox on 2026-08-08, not
from a CI runner — the first honest measurement this configuration has ever had, since nothing
in the repo ran it before today. That sandbox blocks outbound GIS hosts, so a few of its 8
local-only rows may be artefacts of THIS environment rather than product breakage. They are
seeded anyway and deliberately: the gate's stale-entry half turns each artefact into a
one-line ledger shrink on the first real runner, which is cheaper and far more legible than
starting empty and reporting 32 'new regressions' that are nothing of the kind.
